title: Degreewise invertibility of two-term free signed Hom-tensor exchange
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme in universe $t$ and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings of universe $\max(u,t+1)$ on its small pro-etale site. Use the module category and its direct-sum total tensor $T$ and product internal Hom $H$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models, def-pur-hom-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $P,I,Q$ be arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-modules. Suppose $Q^k=0$ for $k\notin\{-1,0\}$ and given isomorphisms identify $Q^{-1}$ and $Q^0$ with the unit module $R$. Let $f:T(H(P,I),Q)\to H(P,T(I,Q))$ be a chain map. Assume that on every site object $U$, for all integers $a,b,p$, sections $v\in H(P,I)^a(U)$, $z\in Q^b(U)$ and $x\in P^p(U)$, evaluation of $f^{a+b}(v\otimes z)$ on $x$ equals $(-1)^{bp}v(x)\otimes z$, using the canonical total-tensor inclusions and reassociation $(p+a)+b=p+(a+b)$. Then for every integer $j$, the module morphism $f^j$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness condition on $P,I$ and no constraint on the differential of $Q$ are imposed.

proof.text: Fix j. The coefficient support removes all summands except b=-1,0 from the direct-sum total tensor, leaving the biproduct of Hom(P,I)^(j+1) tensor Q^(-1) and Hom(P,I)^j tensor Q^0. Use the two unit isomorphisms to remove these tensor factors.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: finite-free quotient construction and coefficient adjunction

proof.text: In degree p+j, I tensor Q is the biproduct of I^(p+j+1) and I^(p+j). Internal Hom from P^p preserves this finite product. Commute the product over all integers p with this two-factor product using their universal properties. No exchange of an infinite sum and product occurs. This gives the same two summands as in the source.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: finite-free quotient construction and coefficient adjunction

proof.text: The coordinate indexed by b=-1 and p is multiplied by (-1)^p, and the b=0 coordinate is unchanged. Squaring these factors gives 1, so the signed coordinate map is invertible. The given local formula identifies f^j with it: equality follows from the tensor universal property, local pure-tensor generation, and Hom product projections, after all restrictions. This also handles zero modules and the empty scheme.

theorem twoTermFreeHomTensor_component_isIso
    (P I Q : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, u} Y R) ℤ)
    (hzero : ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ -1 → k ≠ 0 → IsZero (Q.X k))
    (eNeg : Q.X (-1) ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
    (eZero : Q.X 0 ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
    (f : ((totalTensor Y R).obj
        (homComplex.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1)} (R := R) P I)).obj Q ⟶
      homComplex.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1)} (R := R) P
        (((totalTensor Y R).obj I).obj Q))
    (hf : IsSignedHomTensor Y R P I Q f) (j : ℤ) : IsIso (f.f j)
